videos.title: Real or fake?
videos.audience: Buyers who want to verify authenticity

scenes.text: Real gold, or fake? Here are five checks the pros use.
Gold and silver aren't magnetic, so a magnet won't stick.
Silver carries heat so well that ice starts melting on it right away.
Tap a coin, and real metal rings for a second or two.
Its weight and size should match the published specifications.
And on a certified bar, the serial number should match the certificate.
Best of all, buy from a dealer you can trust.
Buy from Bullion Trading.

videos.title: From spot to store
videos.audience: Buyers curious how bullion is priced

scenes.text: What actually sets the price of a gold bar?
It starts with spot: the live market price, traded nearly around the clock, from Sunday evening to Friday afternoon.
Then a premium covers what it takes to make it and move it: refining, minting, insurance, and shipping.
Our prices are built from live quotes plus a transparent premium, and reprice within minutes when spot moves.
Follow gold, silver, platinum, and palladium on our live charts.

videos.title: Bullion tax, state by state
videos.audience: US buyers asking about sales tax

scenes.text: Will you pay sales tax on gold and silver? That depends on your state.
Investment bullion is tax-free in most states. Collector coins are usually taxed, and jewelry always is.
Some states set a minimum. In New York, qualifying orders of a thousand dollars or more are tax-free.
Find your state in our plain-English bullion tax guide.

scenes.text: There's no single answer, because preferences change.
Our owner has spent more than thirty years in precious metals, and has watched it happen.
Years ago, buyers favored government coins, especially the Canadian Gold Maple Leaf: twenty-four karat, point nine nine nine nine fine.

gold maple leaf

scenes.text: Then many moved to the American Gold Eagle. A little alloy makes it harder and more scratch-resistant, and it still holds a full troy ounce of gold.
Over roughly the past year, one-ounce bars have overtaken coins with our customers, along with smaller gram bars.

one-ounce

scenes.text: Eagles remain highly recognizable and liquid. The best choice depends on the premium, how much you're buying, and your preference.

videos.title: How much over spot?
source: Owner FAQ supplied by the client (Oct 2026)

scenes.text: How much over spot should you really pay for gold?
caption: overspot
over spot

scenes.text: There's no fixed premium. It can change throughout the day.
We constantly compare prices across the bullion market, and adjust for competition, inventory, and supply and demand.
The same item might be fifty dollars over spot in the morning, thirty a few hours later, and eighty or ninety later that day.
When a dealer has plenty of Gold Eagles or one-ounce bars, the premium may drop to move that inventory.
caption: gold eagles
Gold Eagles
one ounce
one-ounce

scenes.text: So it isn't a permanent markup. The market largely sets it.
To judge a premium, compare what reputable dealers charge for that exact product, at that moment.

videos.audience: New York buyers who want their metal today
source: Owner FAQ supplied by the client (Oct 2026)

scenes.text: Can you buy gold online and pick it up in Manhattan the same day?
Sometimes. It depends on how you pay.
With a physical office in Midtown Manhattan, you can arrange to pick up your bullion in person.
For same-day pickup, a bank check is usually easiest. Come in, confirm your purchase and price, and tell us which bank you'll use.
Come back with the bank check, and once we verify it, we can usually release your bullion that same day.
A wire transfer typically means a two-day wait. A personal or business check is held until it clears, generally about five business days. And credit card orders generally must be shipped.
If same-day pickup matters, contact us before you come in.

scenes.text: This October, gold is trading above four thousand dollars an ounce. And one cheap metal weighs almost exactly the same. Tungsten.

scenes.text: Now picture this. You find a one-ounce gold bar online, two hundred dollars under spot. Sealed. A serial number. A five-star seller. You tap buy.

scenes.text: It arrives. The weight checks out. A magnet won't stick. But under a thin skin of gold, it's tungsten.
So who takes the loss? Not the seller. They're gone. You.
You paid three thousand, nine hundred and sixty-five dollars. What you're holding is worth almost nothing.
